about.title: Colton Product Liability Claims
about.longDescription: Colton residents rely on everyday products — tools, vehicle parts, household appliances, machinery used near the rail yards and industrial corridors along I-215 and I-10 — and most of the time they work as expected. When they don't, the results can be serious. A malfunctioning part, a missing warning label, or a manufacturing flaw can turn an ordinary task into a trip to the emergency room. California law allows injured people to pursue compensation from manufacturers, distributors, or retailers without having to prove anyone was careless — the defect itself can be enough. LawProactive helps Colton residents move quickly by connecting them with an independent attorney familiar with product liability claims, who can evaluate what happened, help preserve the product as evidence, and explain your options. This connection service is free, and there's never a fee unless the attorney recovers something for you.

items.title: Strict Liability Can Simplify Your Case
items.desc: California generally lets you focus on proving the product was defective and caused harm, rather than proving the manufacturer was negligent.

items.title: Multiple Parties May Share Responsibility
items.desc: Manufacturers, distributors, and retailers can all potentially be held liable, which may open more than one path toward recovery.

items.title: Guidance on Preserving Evidence
items.desc: An attorney can advise you early on how to keep the product intact, since it's often the most important evidence in a defect claim.

items.question: What should I do with the product that hurt me?
items.answer: Don't throw it away, repair it, or let anyone else alter it. Store it safely and take photos before an attorney or expert examines it, since the physical product is often the strongest evidence in a defect claim.

items.question: Do I need to prove the manufacturer was careless?
items.answer: Not necessarily. Under California's strict liability rules, you generally need to show the product was defective and that the defect caused your injury, not that the company acted negligently.

items.question: Is this connected to Colton's crash data on I-215 or I-10?
items.answer: Not directly — product liability claims involve defective goods rather than the roadway collisions tracked in Colton's traffic reports. That said, if a vehicle part failure contributed to a crash on a corridor like I-215 or I-10, it could raise both product liability and injury claims worth discussing with an attorney.

items.question: How much does it cost to get connected with an attorney?
items.answer: Nothing upfront. LawProactive's connection service is free, and attorneys in the network typically work on contingency, meaning they only get paid if you recover compensation.
